ig_carousel_topic.topic: Public money vs. sharp money, how to tell which is moving the line
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Public money moves lines.
So does sharp money.
They don't move them the same way.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors assume a line moves because 'the public' hammered one side. That's true sometimes. But it misses the more important move.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: Sharp money is a small number of bets placed by high-volume, high-accuracy accounts. Sportsbooks track those accounts. When they bet, the book moves immediately, sometimes before ticket count even tilts.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Example: 80% of tickets are on the favorite. The line moves toward the underdog anyway. That's the book reacting to sharp liability, not public volume. The dog is getting smarter money despite fewer bets.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: Reverse line movement is the tell. Line goes against ticket flow, sharps are likely on the other side. It's not a guarantee. It's a signal worth tracking.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Line moving the wrong direction? That's usually not an accident. Public ticket % vs. line direction is one of the cleaner signals in the market.
